Loss of fdeC causes accumulation of the FdeE product, which in wild type is dioxygenated and cleaved at the A-ring; with the VOC extradiol dioxygenase superfamily fold this supports a dioxygenase activity incorporating both oxygen atoms. No substrate-specific GO term exists, and the evidence (mutant phenotype, not purified enzyme) does not reach a narrower catechol-type term, so the dioxygenase reaction-class term is used, matching the PP_3197 review.

FdeC carries out a catalytic step of the pathway (ring cleavage), so it participates in, rather than merely being required for, flavonoid breakdown. GO defines flavonoid catabolic process as "The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of flavonoids, a group of phenolic derivatives containing a flavan skeleton".

FdeE itself performs the first step of the pathway (the C-8 monooxygenation), so this is participation, not merely necessity. GO defines flavonoid catabolic process as "The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of flavonoids, a group of phenolic derivatives containing a flavan skeleton", which covers naringenin degradation to oxaloacetate.

The conserved locus and orthology identify a candidate FdeH protein, but cupin membership and an associated locus do not identify its catalytic, structural or accessory contribution. The available whole-operon phenotype, including the probably polar fdeA insertion, does not show which step this individual protein performs. There is no independently assayed donor for this particular role; the corresponding BRADU comparator bll6423 likewise carries no process assertion. Retain the original source payload and row position while withdrawing the active proposal. The retired flag records this curator decision, not disappearance of an upstream GOA row or proof of biological absence. Native participation remains an open question.

KEGG assigns PP_3197 to FdeC orthology group K26181, and the report finds strong whole-protein similarity to the experimentally characterized Herbaspirillum FdeC. GO lacks a term for the exact naringenin-intermediate A-ring cleavage, so the most specific supported extradiol-dioxygenase parent is used.

K26181/R13075 pathway placement and orthology to experimentally tested Hsero_1005 support flavonoid catabolism. GO:0046275 flavonoid catabolic process is used; GO has no naringenin-specific catabolic child.

The locus, K26179 assignment and Rieske architecture identify a candidate, but neither PP_3198 nor Hsero_1006 has an established physiological electron donor, acceptor or flavonoid-catabolic step. Purified FdeE works without added FdeD; that does not exclude another role, but it supplies no positive evidence of participation by FdeD. The same-role comparators Hsero_1006 and bll6426 likewise decline a process assertion. Retain this inherited row for provenance while marking the proposal as over-annotation; cluster binding remains supported and native pathway involvement remains a knowledge gap. No assertion of biological absence is made. The retired flag records deliberate withdrawal of this curator-authored proposal from the active set; it does not report disappearance of an upstream GOA annotation.

PP_3199 and the experimentally characterized Hsero_1007/FdeE monooxygenase are reciprocal proteome best hits, share 40.4% global identity, and occur in conserved fde loci. GO:0046275 flavonoid catabolic process is used; GO has no naringenin-specific catabolic child.

The target aligns to genetically characterized HERSS FdeC with 59.9% identity across 96.8% of its residues, shares the VOC scaffold, and occupies the corresponding conserved catabolic locus. FdeC-mutant accumulation of the hydroxylated precursor supports oxygenolytic ring cleavage together with its extradiol architecture. This supports a reaction-class ISS inference without requiring a purified BRADU assay. It does not establish exact substrate, product, metal, or native pathway flux, nor refute the unresolved glyoxalase-I prediction. No original row or proposed term is an ancestor or descendant of this dioxygenase class.
